Title: "or" phrases (e.g. Society of Leopold, Blade Clot)

Messages.Author: Hakuron
Messages.Body:
This one is about "or" phrases ... Examples:
>
> Society of Leopold
>
> Unique master.
> Put this card on a vampire. During his or her controller's untap phase, the vampire with this card either burns 1 blood or is burned (the controller's choice). The vampire with this card can move it to any other vampire as a +1 stealth  action.
>
> Blade Clot
>
> Requires an anarch.
> Only usable when this anarch diablerizes a vampire with capacity 7 or more. Put this card in play with 3 clot counters. When an anarch you control inflicts hand or melee weapon damage, you may move a clot counter from this card to the opposing minion. A minion with a clot counter goes to torpor or is burned during his or her untap phase. If an older vampire rescues the vampire, burn the clot counter.
>
Question: Is the controlling methuselah allowed to choose the first part of the "or" phrase (e.g. burn 1 blood, go to torpor) even if the given vampire cannot "fulfil" it (since e.g. he has no blood, is already in torpor)?

Thanks in advance!

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
Because you must have a blood to be able to burn it, while you can send to torpor something which is in torpor. In essence, both work the same way, but you can alway send the vampire in torpor, while you may be unable to burn blood on him.

MtG have the same thing where you can tap a tapped permanent, while you cannot sacrifice a card who is have been sacrificied before.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Hakuron wrote:
> Am I really "allowed" to voluntarily burn a clotted vampire?
>
Yes, you have a choice.
>
> Unlike "Society of Leopold", "Blade Clot" misses the addition "controller's choice" ...
>
Even if it's not always the case, the parenthesis indicate here that it's just a reminder text.

"During X, do Y or Z" is the pattern of a choice happening once during X.
If you can't do Y, you're bound to do Z.
If you can't do Z, you're bound to do Y.
If you can do neither, you're "stuck".

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Correct answers from jamesatzehphyr and Ankha.

In both cases (Society of Leopold, Blade Clot), cardtext reads "do X or do Y". You're free to do whichever you want, but you must do one of them. Burning blood from a vampire with no blood wouldn't meet the "this vampire burns 1 blood" text.
